what_matters.tag_note: Aixtron · Thursday, and after the close
what_matters.head: Aixtron fell 12.7% in Frankfurt on Thursday, 3.3 times its usual day. Half an hour after the close it said its third-quarter orders and profit were well above expectations.
what_matters.detail: Investing.com put the fall down to the worldwide chip sell-off and found no company news. At 18:00 Frankfurt time Aixtron put preliminary Q3 orders at about €275M, against the €214.6M median analyst estimate it cited, and operating profit at about €57M, a 31% margin, helped by product mix. Revenue was about €184M. Its full-year forecast is unchanged, and the full Q3 statement is due on 29 Oct. Not in Thursday's Frankfurt price.

what_matters.head: The 10-year Treasury yield fell about 10 basis points to 5.09% on Thursday, twice its usual day and its biggest one-day fall in over a year. US producer prices rose 1.3% in September, the most since March 2022.
what_matters.detail: Investing.com said money left tech shares and tech companies' debt for government bonds as the cost of insuring that debt against default rose. Reuters said Fed officials had signalled they could wait for a clearer picture before the 27–28 Oct meeting, after markets had put the chance of an October rate rise at about 50% following Wednesday's consumer prices. The US dollar index fell 0.5%, 1.7 times its usual day, from an 18-month high on Wednesday.

what_matters.head: TSMC now expects revenue to grow about 44% in US dollars this year, up from its earlier 'slightly above 40%'. It kept its US$60–64B capex plan for 2026.
what_matters.detail: Chief executive C.C. Wei did not confirm the 2027 price rise reported in the press; he said its pricing is 'very strategic' and depends on the product, location and technology. The finance chief expects the hit to gross margin from its overseas factories to widen to 3–4% over the next few years. Thursday was the first US session after the results.

latest.tape_note: US stocks steadied on Thursday after Wednesday's fall: the Dow rose more than 1% and the S&P 500 0.3%, and the Nasdaq ended little changed after being down more than 1% during the day. The Philadelphia chip index fell for an eighth straight day, its longest losing run since October 2008, but trimmed its losses late in the day. Oil rose 3.0% and gold 1.5%. The US dollar fell 0.2% against the Singapore dollar.

recent.headline: Aixtron fell 12.7% in Frankfurt on Thursday, 3.3 times its usual day. Half an hour after the close it said its third-quarter orders and profit were well above expectations.

Chip and AI stocks fell hard on Wednesday. US consumer prices rose more than expected in September, which raised bets on another Fed rate rise, and worries about how AI data centres are paid for spread.
MAS left its Singapore-dollar policy unchanged this morning. All 10 analysts in a Reuters poll last week had expected it to tighten again, after a very slight tightening in July.

SK Hynix fell about 9% and Samsung about 8% by 13:05 Seoul time, after China's CXMT said it plans to launch a denser kind of server memory by the end of 2026. The Kospi was down 7.2% around midday, its lowest level since July.
SK Hynix was down about 4.0% and Samsung about 3.2% at 13:05 Seoul time, in Korea's first session since Thursday. The 5.0% and 4.0% falls shown below are too large.
